method: Static analysis only: atomscan slow/no-update/no-follow, cleave facts, rizin native disassembly, dnfile/dncil managed disassembly, safe resource extraction and arithmetic-only JavaScript decoder reconstruction. No sample, installer or plugin was executed.

samples.identity: Host Probe, unsigned Go 1.26.2 hostprobe development build; collected as Ghost_netcheck.exe
execution: main.main (0x140100100) parses operator targets and probe options, expands IP/CIDR/range input, deduplicates and shuffles addresses, creates result directory/file, starts rate-limited workers and a progress reporter. Defaults: TCP port 445, timeout 200 ms, 500 workers, unlimited rate unless specified.
main.loadTargets (0x1400fc200) reads command-line targets or a line-based operator-selected input file. main.expandCIDR and main.expandRange expand address ranges.
main.main.func5 (0x140100d20) receives target addresses, waits for optional rate tokens, invokes main.tcpProbe and records responsive addresses through outputWriter.writeAlive.

main.tcpProbe (0x1400fc960) formats the target endpoint and calls net.DialTimeout at 0x1400fca39. On success it closes the connection and returns true. It sends no SMB authentication, exploit or encryption payload.

Results are written locally as alive_<timestamp>.txt, with an optional output override and quiet console mode. Go runtime thread-context APIs are runtime/preemption support, not an injection path. No external rendezvous, embedded second stage, signature or overlay was found.
samples.judgement: The exact hash is submitted by SOCRadar STRU to ThreatFox as part of its INC/Gentlemen offensive-infrastructure investigation. Combined with the custom SMB-default range reconnaissance implementation, this tips the operational judgement to malicious tooling. The binary alone implements a dual-use TCP scanner and is not an INC encryptor or Ghost C2 implant. No victim targets, invocation or proof of deployment accompany this copy.
samples.coverage: One suspicious reconnaissance composite plus two notable interface observations added. The requested two suspicious/four hostile minimum cannot be supported: only one suspicious behavior class is established. Randomized scan order, quiet output and local result logging do not independently prove evasion or theft. No duplicate or invented attack traits were added.

execution: CLR entry token 0x06000072 hosts System.Management.Automation in-process, reads embedded Sleipnir.ps1 (364937 bytes) and passes it to PowerShell.AddScript/BeginInvoke. Credential-dialog and keyboard methods are PS2EXE host interface implementations; no application credential harvesting was found.

The readable script opens a WPF window. Initial callbacks collect local performance/security state; profile and individual-tweak buttons call Invoke-TweakApply. It checks compatibility, saves prior state, applies the selected change, verifies the result and writes local history. Closing the window stops runspaces/timers and exits.

Gaming/maximum profiles really add Defender exclusions for game paths and game process names. Other selected tweaks disable HVCI/VBS, hypervisor launch or CPU mitigations, change services, startup approvals, DNS, caches and game configuration. These are meaningful security effects and their accurate detections remain.

Kill lists target Discord, Steam/browser/cloud-sync and launcher applications for performance. FocusGuard is an opt-in foreground-window hook to keep a game focused; it registers a user hotkey, minimizes intruding windows and restores the selected game. No keyboard logging or remote command channel was found.

Driver actions use configured AMD/NVIDIA/Intel vendor URLs. NVIDIA/Intel install requests download to a local file, require Get-AuthenticodeSignature Status=Valid and the expected publisher, require a successful restore point, then start the downloaded installer. Current NVIDIA/Intel URLs are HTML support pages, so this install path fails signature checks. The source comment promises no cross-host redirects, but Invoke-WebRequest does not enforce that claim; it was not treated as a verified safeguard.

The bare-script elevation branch requests normal UAC consent. Its remote IRM/IEX branch is guarded by a placeholder-URL check and is not configured here; the compiled requireAdministrator manifest supplies elevation before script execution. Startup/task references inspect or toggle existing entries, with no hidden self-install path found.
samples.packaging: Authenticode file digest is intact (198fc01289e38f1072d6daaa62cf53be32c8558d477ebbda5d56042270b722f2). The signing leaf is self-issued CN=Sleipnir Local Publisher. osslsigncode confirms matching current/calculated digest and a valid DigiCert timestamp, but rejects the signer trust chain as self-signed. Integrity is not authenticated vendor trust.
external_checks: NVIDIA URL resolves to its official driver-download page; Intel URL is its official Driver & Support Assistant page.
The AMD URL returned an AMD Download-Incomplete redirect; no driver payload was supplied by that response.
No configured third-party payload host or covert data upload was found.
samples.judgement: The selected security weakening is real, but it is disclosed and wired to the tuning interface rather than a concealed attack. Backups, restores, state verification, fixed game exclusions and installer verification support the declared purpose. The self-signed wrapper, administrative PowerShell, exclusions and mitigation changes plausibly explain heuristic collection; the original collection circumstances remain unknown. Retain the suspicious Defender process-exclusion finding. BENIGN is a sighted-quarantine judgement, not ground-truth provenance.

samples.identity: Atom's Connections 1.7.1 beta, Ultra Encode, LLC; unsigned .NET/PeerJS messaging application
execution: All 17 managed methods were disassembled. Main calls Run, which binds only 127.0.0.1/localhost:47800 by default, opens the local URL using the desktop shell and serves a fixed route table.

LoadFiles verifies app.pak SHA-256 db2fd6b4dc620bdddf8cad94e451514066e9cd8181f40ba9a4905159800ccc3c, decompresses gzip and reads length-prefixed resources into memory. Members: index.html (616829 bytes), player.html (5019), vendor/peerjs.min.js (92865). No loaded assembly or dropped executable exists in this path.

The device key is generated by RandomNumberGenerator and saved with DPAPI CurrentUser. It protects the application vault, not another application credential store. /device-key and /save require POST, X-Atoms:1 and non-cross-site Fetch Metadata. The Host header is restricted to the local listeners.

SafeTarget limits save paths to app subdirectories of Pictures/Documents, rejects traversal/reserved names and checks canonical root containment. EndOtherCopies is reached after a port conflict and terminates only other copies with the same executable basename and configured port. HKCU atoms: URL registration and a desktop shortcut launch the same executable; neither supplies a login trigger.

The main script uses a 2507-entry custom-Base64 string table, rotated 163 positions, and 1140 pure arithmetic decoder wrappers. 10968 constant decoder calls were replaced without executing the application. Player rotation was separately decoded (43 positions); it permits YouTube/Vimeo playback messages from expected origins and a fixed command set.

Decoded session code uses identity plus ephemeral ECDH P-256, HKDF and AES-GCM. It binds identities to public-key hashes, checks frame sequencing and dispatches contact/invitation-based posts, chat, groups, file chunks, calls and plugins. Microphone/camera requests belong to call/device UI paths. No native-command dispatch, credential harvesting or covert host survey was found.

Update metadata is fetched from the publisher and produces a user-clicked download link. Plugin catalog entries are path/size/hash checked; packages run in allow-scripts frames without same-origin authority and with connections/frames denied by CSP. Additional app-mediated permissions default off.
external_checks: Bundled PeerJS is byte-identical to upstream 1.5.4, SHA-256 ad5d8870d1e389914f9cba8d35be313c4327c69ee0a221e482e9bf7621136fe5.
Publisher site describes the same product. version.json currently advertises 1.11.0 released 2026-10-20 with a same-origin installer; it is not an exact reference build for this older sample.

Current catalog downloads Neon Arcade 1.1.1 and Atom Math Lab 1.4.0 were fetched and their advertised SHA-256 values verified. Their archive contents implement games/UI/assets and arithmetic exercises with app-helper messages, not a native payload.
samples.judgement: Recovered native/managed/web behavior agrees with the visible messaging purpose. Unsigned packaging, near-maximum gzip-resource entropy, obfuscated scripts, DPAPI, COM shortcut creation, process termination and peer networking plausibly explain generic/ML detections. No abusive peer configuration or invocation is supplied. Genuine obfuscation remains suspicious even with a BENIGN sighted-quarantine verdict.

rule_changes.expanded: Existing parseint-decoder-loop and plain-javascript-obfuscator-string-array-runtime now cover HTML inline scripts. No duplicated obfuscator signature was added.
rule_changes.narrowed: push-shift-bracket-pattern and parseint-decoder-loop ignore HTML comments. The unsupported claim was decoder behavior inferred from commented-out script text. A comment-only control demonstrates the benign match; real obfuscated script elements still fire.
rule_changes.consumers: Inspected exact shared-rule references and representative wallet, WSH, browser anti-debug, obfuscated loader and declared-build consumers. Existing JS/TS scopes and required attack legs remain. Before/after comparison used a hard-linked scratch ruleset with the original tracked shared YAML restored; no working-tree rules were replaced during comparison.

verification.focused_controls: Persisted check.py passed all 8 assertions: real compiled Go CIDR/TCP scanner positive, single-host checker negative, range-only interface negative, inline rotated decoder positive, ordinary queue negative, no-rotation negative, comment-only decoder negative for both composite and rotation atom.
verification.retained_attacks: All findings retained on external-batch fixtures obfuscated-remote-channel-follow.js, concealed-wallet.js, rc4-multiline-loader.js (including its decoded layer) and dist-index.js. Declared-build and undeclared-build severity controls both passed.
verification.losses: No findings lost from any supplied executable, extracted HTML or bundled PeerJS. No attack findings lost in regression controls. Comment-only HTML loses the incorrect rotation observation. The no-rotation synthetic page loses three baseline HTML/extension display findings when a new notable observation is present, an engine low-tier projection effect; those matchers were untouched.
verification.resource_limit: The PE scan does not automatically expose the gzip managed-resource web assets as archive members. They were extracted and rescanned separately. This remains an analyzer extraction gap, not a YAML suppression.
verification.final_validation: Run make validate as the final task action; terminal outcome is authoritative.

classifier_disagreements: Host Probe remains unflagged by the calibrated model (level -1) despite MALICIOUS operational judgement. Probability increases from 0.23115508 to 0.7797581 and the new suspicious range-scan finding is present.

The extracted, benign media-player HTML becomes model-flagged at level 1 (probability 0.9995355) after accurate inline-obfuscation coverage. Its former probability was 0.9247735 at level -1. Keep the true obfuscation finding and report the classifier false positive.
Sleipnir retains its accurate suspicious Defender exclusion signal with a BENIGN verdict. The supplied PE remains model-unflagged; its probability is unchanged.
